q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution

NVIDIA reports its Q2 FY2027 earnings typically in late May or early June of the following fiscal year. Since today is August 23, 2026, and the question asks about forward guidance issued *in* the Q2 FY2027 earnings release, this guidance would typically be announced around June 2026 or possibly delayed into early-to-mid 2027 depending on exact fiscal calendar timing.

However, the research provided explicitly states that NVIDIA issued forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 on May 20, 2026 (which is before today's date of August 23, 2026). This means the guidance has already been released.

**The resolution appears to already have occurred.** NVIDIA provided forward guidance of $91.0 billion ±2% for Q2 FY2027.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The forward guidance of $91.0 billion ±2% was already issued on May 20, 2026. This translates to a range of approximately $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion. The most likely outcome is that the actual Q2 FY2027 revenue will fall within or very close to this guided range, as companies typically provide conservative guidance they can achieve.

The research notes that Wall Street analysts' average estimate is $91.9 billion, which sits above the midpoint but within the guided range. NVIDIA's guidance explicitly excludes China Data Center compute revenue, which may create some upside if restrictions ease, but the company is clearly being cautious.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Demand weakness in AI/data center acceleration (though Q1 showed strong momentum)
- Macro economic contraction reducing customer capex spending
- More stringent export restrictions to China than currently anticipated
- Supply chain issues affecting production/delivery
- Loss of major customer orders

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Accelerated AI adoption across cloud providers and enterprises
- Better-than-expected utilization of new products (Hopper/Blackwell variants)
- Easing of China export restrictions allowing incremental revenue
- Share gains from competitors
- Lower gross margins on higher volume (revenue beat with margin pressure)
- Strength in adjacent segments (professional visualization, automotive)

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- Q1 FY2027 (ended April 26, 2026): $81.6 billion actual revenue, up 20% sequentially
- Q2 FY2027 forward guidance: $91.0 billion ±2%
- This implies ~12% sequential growth from Q1 to Q2 (or $9.4B sequential increase)
- Wall Street consensus: $91.9 billion

The base rate context: NVIDIA has demonstrated strong sequential growth recently (20% Q0→Q1), though Q1→Q2 guidance suggests moderation to ~12% sequential growth. This is reasonable given the law of large numbers.

---

## Probability Distribution Estimate

Given that guidance has already been issued at $91.0B ±2% ($89.2B–$92.8B), and assuming the question is asking where the actual Q2 FY2027 revenue will fall:

**The most likely outcome is that NVIDIA will hit within or very close to its own guidance range.** Companies rarely miss their own forward guidance significantly (though upside surprises are more common than downside).

The distribution should be:
- **Peak probability around $91.0B** (the midpoint of guidance)
- **Wider tail toward upside** (~$93-95B range) — NVIDIA tends to beat slightly
- **Modest downside tail** (~$88-89B range) — less likely given conservative guidance practices

Considering:
- The range specified (99.5-115.5B) is well above current guidance
- Wall Street consensus at $91.9B is slightly above midpoint but within guidance
- Historical pattern of NVIDIA meeting/modestly beating guidance
- Conservative guidance approach (zero China revenue assumed)

The question's range appears designed to test whether NVIDIA will significantly exceed current guidance. This is possible but requires ~9-25% upside from guidance midpoint.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, predicts $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This guidance implies a range between approximately $89.2 billion and $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

This Q2 FY2027 outlook does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). For comparison, in Q1 FY2027 (ended April 26, 2026), NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion, up 20% sequentially and 85% year-over-year, with Data Center revenue reaching $75.2 billion [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). Wall Street analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is around $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), which falls within NVIDIA's provided range.
